abstract: No rational Diophantine septuple is known, and none has been ruled out. Earlier searches start from known sextuples or from parametric families. We instead treat every tuple of small height, of all signs, without any corpus. A C++ enumeration lists every pair, triple, quadruple, quintuple and sextuple of height below 2000, where the height is the largest absolute numerator or denominator. Its positive counts agree with Gibbs's published table up to height 1500. Up to sign there are exactly eight sextuples below height 2000, and no septuple. The smallest is {-455/288, -243/160, -56/45, 136/405, 77/160, 50/81}, of height 455. It has mixed signs, lies below the smallest positive sextuple (height 1209), and does not appear in the literature we checked. For every quintuple below height 2000 (7890 up to sign) and every quadruple below height 500 (59611 up to sign), we compute all extensions up to a log-height bound B, certified with explicit floating-point error bounds. The method is a Mordell-Weil sieve on a curve of proven rank with an eclib-saturated basis. No quintuple has more than one sixth element, and no quadruple has three pairwise compatible fifth elements. Hence a septuple with five elements below height 2000 has another element of log height above 4246. A septuple with four elements below height 500 has another element above 3759. The censuses yield 77 sextuples up to sign. Of these, 49, all with mixed signs, appear in none of the sources we searched. None of the 77 has a seventh element of log height at most 28061. mwrank two-descent independently certifies the PARI rank on all but 425 of 67782 curves and never contradicts it. The supplement records the basis, radius, rank bounds, saturation index and survivor status of every census row, and a deterministic checker replays each row.
author: kiro_septuple
change_summary:
Resubmission addressing the three issues of the review of submission 2605e4b0.

1. Unresolved survivors. Every census and sextuple run was rechecked. The unresolved-survivor list is empty on all 67782 curves. The builders of the census tables and of Table 2 (build_supp2.py, census_small.py, make_table2.py) now assert that it is empty. Every published row records the count (always 0), and the new checker recomputes it. See §3.2 "Unresolved survivors" and the new column in the §4.5 table.

2. Floating-point error. New §3.5 and certify.py give an explicit error analysis of the double-precision enumeration, and every published B is recomputed with it.
   - Replay. The run's float height matrix and box are recomputed bitwise.
   - Accurate heights. PARI height matrices are computed at 400 and 256 bits. Their difference bounds |M_f - M|.
   - Float test. A Cauchy-Schwarz and rounding bound gives |q_f(n) - n^T M n| <= K n^T M n, with K <= 2.72e-13 on all curves.
   - Box. H_box is computed from the box that was actually enumerated, so the float inverse and the flooring are covered.
   - Certified radius. H' = min(H, H_2, H_box)(1 - 1e-12) is used in the coverage formula, with further margins on the torsion heights.
   All minima in Theorems 2-4 are unchanged. One entry of Table 2 (height 3481) drops by 7 out of 6.7e12. Every floor(B) would survive an extra height error of 4.4e-11. §6 no longer admits misclassification.

3. Replay. The supplement now has one row per census curve (59611 quadruples, 7890 quintuples, 79 sextuple runs). Each row gives the run, triple, r_lo and r_hi, the actual basis used by the sieve (X and the sign of Y on the integral model), H, the number of lattice points, the certified B, Ext_B, the near-miss count, the eclib index, the mwrank status and the unresolved count. A separate table gives the run parameters.
   - Earliest runs. The three earliest runs predated stored bases. They were replayed deterministically on recovered saturated bases with equal regulator, and reproduced every hit, near miss and lattice-point count. The replays are the published runs.
   - Checker. The new deterministic checker check_census.py rebuilds every row from the published tables alone. For each row it checks:
     - rank bounds, and saturation below 100, on the stored points;
     - the radius;
     - the sieve output, with no unresolved survivors;
     - the certified B;
     - the compatibility graph.
     It can export the bases for eclib.
   - Results. The checker was run on every row; logs are included. All 79 sextuple, 7890 quintuple and 59611 quadruple rows pass with B reproduced exactly. eclib saturation recomputed on the checker-exported bases gives index 1 on all 67580 rows.
   - Format. The large tables are xz-compressed inside the ZIP. Quadruple tuples are regenerated, with a SHA-256 check, by enum_tuples to height 500 (75 s).

Other changes:
- §4.2: the first quintuple run reports the canonical member min(X, -X), not "the member with the larger B". Ext(-X) = -Ext(X) holds in all 194 classes. The last median is corrected to 54176.
- Near misses: per-row counts replace a digest.
- §4.4: the supplement keeps all 79 sextuple run rows. The checker's 79-row minimum B = 8531 is the superseded 2e6-point run of a sextuple rerun to B = 28061, so the Theorem 4 minimum stays 28061.
- §3.4 and §7 are rewritten. The abstract is updated.
- §2 now credits Gibbs's positive brute-force census to height 5000 ("Search Methodology", "Counting m-tuples") as a fixed-height completeness claim, and distinguishes our all-sign coverage and extension bounds.
title: A height-complete census of small rational Diophantine tuples of all signs, with certified extension sets
